newsitem.title: TURKEY: Demirdokum says to exceed sales target.
newsitem.headline: Demirdokum says to exceed sales target.

text.p: Turkish heating goods producer Turk Demir Dokum Fabrikalari A.S. will exceed its 27 percent sales growth target in 1997 based on early results, a senior company official said.

"It seems that we will exceed our 27 percent growth target in real terms because of the soaring demand in the first half of the year," Orhan Ercek, deputy general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Total sales of the company, which makes boiler, heaters and radiators, were 15.77 trillion lira (then $190 million) last year.
Shares of the company rose to 7,100 on Friday morning from a close of 6,900 on Thursday.

"Demand has soared because of last year's stagnation, when we could grow only by eight percent," he added. Company sales grew 38 percent in 1995. In the 1990s as a whole annual growth of the company has averaged 25 percent.

Demirdokum reported 5.31 trillion lira turnover in the first quarter of 1997, against 2.38 trillion lira a year earlier. Net profit increased to 106 billion lira from 34 billion lira on the same comparison.

"The speed of heating and boiling equipment renewal in Turkey is very high because of the changing structure of family housing," Ercek said. He said many buildings were switching from communal heating systems to central heating for individual flats, fuelling sales of instant water boilers and radiators.

Ercek said they would exceed sales targets for all products except those using natural gas. "Work on gas distribution is slower than expected and we will barely reach sales targets for those products," he said.
Demirdokum aims to increase exports by more than 30 percent to $30 milion in 1997 from $23 million in 1996.

"Our export growth target is higher than the total sales target because we want to increase the share of exports in all products," Ercek said. The company exports 50 percent of its panel radiators and aims to have the same export level in all products.
The company's main export markets are Britain, Germany and Italy, where it has warehouses and marketing companies. "This year our target markets are France and Spain," he said.
He said technological advances had given Demirdokum a cost advantage over Turkish and European companies. "We have the latest technology which aids cheaper production."
Ercek said Demirdokum's investment activities were boosted by 30 to 40 percent annual growth in the domestic market, while European rivals had growth of just one to five percent in their own markets.
Demirdokum has made considerable investments in capacity expansion over the last five years, covering all products including panel radiators to the year 2000.
"Soaring demand for panel radiators in the European markets led us to invest in the product," Ercek said.
Demirdokum has an annual production capacity of 750,000 metres for panel radiators currently and will increase this to 900,000 metres in 1997 and 1.2 million metres in 1998.
Total investment spending will be $15 million including capacity expansion in panel radiators and modernisation in other product lines.
